LayoutDef.description:
How the planner lays out a dungeon of this type (architecture 15.3): the entrance, a main path of rooms a
player passes through, the room that ends it, and side branches off the main path, each ending in a dead end.
The planner closes every connector left over with a dead end or a wall, so a layout has more rooms than these
counts.

branch_rooms.description: [min, max] rooms in each branch, its dead end included (1 to 8).
branch_rooms.title: Branch Rooms

branches.description: [min, max] side branches off the main path (0 to 16).
branches.title: Branches

ending.description: The role of the room that ends the main path: the boss's lair or a treasury.
ending.title: Ending

main_path.description: [min, max] rooms between the entrance and the ending (1 to 96).
main_path.title: Main Path

pacing.description: If set, the rhythm of corridors, features and fights along the main path, and the treasure at the end of each branch (RLM-364). Unset: any room that fits a slot may take it.

walls.description: If set, the planner may close a leftover doorway with a wall instead of a dead end (RLM-364).

LayoutDef.title: LayoutDef

LocalizedText.description: A player-facing text, keyed by locale. Realmforge ships English only, so en_us is the one locale.
LocalizedText.title: LocalizedText

PacingDef.description:
The rhythm of a layout (RLM-364, architecture 15.3): on the main path, a fight (a combat room with a spawner)
once a gap drawn from ``fights`` lies behind the last one, else a feature (a combat room without one) after a run
of corridors drawn from ``corridors``; the branches are corridors up to a treasure room.

corridors.description: [min, max] corridors in a row on the main path before a feature or a fight (1 to 8), drawn binomially (RLM-364).
corridors.title: Corridors

fights.description: [min, max] rooms, corridors and features, between two fights on the main path (1 to 16), drawn binomially: [2, 4] gives 2 a quarter of the time, 3 half, 4 a quarter (RLM-364).
fights.title: Fights

repeat.description: Rooms of distance from the entrance the planner tries to keep between two copies of a room that is no corridor, and between two locks (rooms with an entry); 0: copies may be neighbours.
repeat.title: Repeat

PacingDef.title: PacingDef

WallsDef.description:
A plain wall that closes a doorway nothing else takes, one block behind it: rf gen builds it as a template of
3 x 3 blocks with one connector and adds it to the dungeon type's rooms with the role ``wall``.

block.description: The block it is built of, e.g. minecraft:stone_bricks.
block.title: Block

weight.description: Its weight among the dead ends that may close a doorway, like a room's weight in its pool.
weight.title: Weight

WallsDef.title: WallsDef

description:
A kind of dungeon: the room pool it is built from, the rules of its layout, the key that opens a portal to it,
how long that portal stays open (W4d) and its base level (RLM-459). Encounters, loot and its theme come with the
tasks that use them.

id.description: Lowercase snake_case id; becomes realmforge:<id>. Must equal the file name.
id.title: Id

key.description: The item that opens a dungeon portal to it, used up each time: its key. One key per dungeon type.
key.title: Key

level.description: Its base level: the level of its boss, where the campaign places it (its chapter and its order in the chapter); a type without a boss names the level its end stands for. A run's level is this base raised to the highest level of its party when it opens, and holds for the run: bosses (#c:bosses) are at it, minibosses (#realmforge:minibosses) one below, every other mob two or three below (RLM-240, RLM-459).
level.title: Level

name.description: The dungeon's name, a label (Title Case).

open_minutes.description: How long a portal to it stays open, in minutes; then everyone inside is sent back (W4d).
open_minutes.title: Open Minutes

pool.description: The room pool it is built from: the rooms whose sidecar lists this id in its pools.
pool.title: Pool

title: DungeonTypeDef
